topic: Neural Network Learning: The Intuitive Backpropagation
target_audience: University students (STEM majors) or tech-curious beginners

sections.title: The Analogy: The Guessing Game
lecture_lines: Neural networks start as simple guessing machines.
They classify inputs into random, wrong categories.
A robot guesses cat versus dog pixels.
animations: Show a simple neural network schematic with nodes initialized to random state. Color nodes #FFFFFF.
Show random, incorrect output classifications (e.g., 'Cat' and 'Dog' labels) flashing in red (#FF0000).
Represent the robot input as a pixel grid (2x2) and highlight guesses fluctuating randomly.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Error Surface
lecture_lines: We visualize error as a mountainous landscape.
Low valleys represent the ideal minimum error.
A ball rolls downhill, seeking the lowest point.
animations: Display a 3D-like mountain landscape (loss surface) in shades of blue (#87CEEB).
Highlight the deep center of the mountain landscape in #00FF00 (green) to represent minimum error.
Show a small ball (represented by a circle) in #FF4500 (orange) rolling from a high peak down toward the green valley.

sections.title: The Core Concept: Backpropagation (The Blame Game)
lecture_lines: Backpropagation is the game of assigning blame.
We trace error backward, layer by layer.
Each neuron receives feedback on its contribution.
animations: Show a multi-layer network with nodes. Text 'Error' appears at the output layer.
Use green (#00FF00) directional arrows to animate signal traveling from the output layer back to the input layer.
Highlight individual neurons in yellow (#FFFF00) as they receive feedback signal and 'blame' value.

sections.title: The Math: Chain Rule in Motion
lecture_lines: The chain rule connects small weight changes.
It acts as a precise mathematical multiplier.
Tiny changes ripple through connected network gears.
animations: Show a series of gears linked together representing weight connections. Color gears #A9A9A9.
Animate gear rotation sequentially using small white (#FFFFFF) tick marks to indicate mathematical multiplication.
Show ripples of light in cyan (#00FFFF) passing through the gear train when one is rotated.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
lecture_lines: Forward pass guesses, calculating initial error.
Backward pass adjusts weights, reducing error.
Repetition makes the network progressively smarter.
animations: Display two panels: 'Forward' with right-pointing arrow, 'Backward' with left-pointing arrow. Color: #FFFFFF.
Animate a loop where 'Forward' results in an 'Error' value, then 'Backward' modifies a weight.
Show a counter of 'Epochs' increasing, with the 'Error' value progressively decreasing and changing color to bright green (#00FF00).
